case_title: DATARAM SINGH v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH & ANR.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.419, s.420, s.406 and s.506; Negotiable Instruments Act s.138
neutral_facts: The accused was alleged to have cheated the complainant of an amount exceeding Rs. 37 lakhs and issued a cheque for Rs. 18 lakhs which was later stopped. The complainant filed an FIR and a complaint case under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code and the Negotiable Instruments Act. During the investigation, the accused was not arrested. The accused approached the High Court for quashing the FIR and was granted time to appear before the trial judge. The accused eventually appeared before the trial judge and was taken into judicial custody. The trial court and High Court rejected the accused's bail applications. The Supreme Court considered the circumstances and held that the accused was not arrested during the investigation, there was no apprehension that he would abscond or interfere with the trial, and that the trial court and High Court should have granted bail.
